lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ricardo Coutinho | Lesson 18 -- Lunch Near the Office
lesson.grammar_point: I'd like / Can I have + a / some / any (countable and uncountable nouns)

listenings.text: Hi Ricardo, it's Amy. Lunch today? There is a good place near the office, the Brickell Deli. The chicken and rice is very good, and the salads are big. I'd like some salad today. Lunch there is from eleven to three, but at one it is very busy. So, twelve thirty? I'm in the lobby at twelve thirty. See you!

Hi, it's Paul. A small piece of advice about lunch in the United States. Lunch here is short. Many people eat at their desk, in thirty minutes. In a restaurant, the plates are very big. Water is free: just ask for some water. At the end, ask for the check. And the tip is not on the check. You write it: fifteen or twenty percent.

extra_audio.text: It is twelve thirty, and I have lunch near the office. I look at the menu. I'd like the chicken and rice, please. Can I have some water? At the end, I ask for the check.
